title: Bounded clean call computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $e\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and let $x$, $a$, and $c$ be Boolean words. Suppose $M$ halts on input word $a$ with output word $c$ after $T$ steps. Then there is a positive natural number $t$ with $t\le (24+13k)(T+|a|+|c|+1)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$, such that the call machine's run from its entry state, with $a$ on tape zero and all other work tapes blank, does not reach its exit state at any time $j<t$. At time $t$ its configuration is the exit-state configuration with $a$ on tape zero and empty output if $e$ is true, and with $c$ on tape zero and output $c$ if $e$ is false; all other work tapes are blank, the input head is at its initial position, and the other configuration data have their initial values.
